title: Can ChatGPT really replace your apps? I tried using the chatbot for 12 everyday tasks on my phone — here’s…
excerpt: I used ChatGPT instead of 12 everyday phone apps to see what it could replace today — and what still works much better with a dedicated app.
content_html:
Apple and OpenAI are currently engaged in a legal battle. Apple alleges that OpenAI stole trade secrets and poached employees.

But the two companies have always had a complicated relationship. They partnered in 2024 to bring ChatGPT to Apple devices, but Apple chose Google's Gemini rather than OpenAI for Siri. Then OpenAI acquired io, the hardware startup founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, and promised a future hardware device, powered by AI.

All of this has prompted speculation about what Apple is worried about if OpenAI makes hardware, too. We can't know the company's motivations and the specifics of the case are still unfolding. But it got me thinking, what if your phone stopped being a collection of apps and instead revolved around AI?

If AI became the main interface, which apps would disappear and which would survive? And would a phone controlled through ChatGPT actually be practical?

So I decided to find out based on the current tech we have. For a day, whenever I reached for an app, I'd try ChatGPT first instead. If it could do the job, great it passed the test. If it couldn't, it would fail.

There were some obvious things I missed out from the start. ChatGPT isn't connected to my email, it can't open WhatsApp for me and it doesn't have access to my wallet, so those wouldn’t be part of the test. But there were plenty of everyday tasks that felt like fair game.

1. Stopwatch

I use the stopwatch in my iPhone's Clock app constantly throughout the day. When I'm working, cooking or exercising, it's one of the simplest ways I've found to keep me on track as a freelancer. When you can set your own schedule, it's way too easy to disappear down a research rabbit hole and lose an hour.

I asked ChatGPT to start a stopwatch. It said it couldn't measure elapsed time, although it could estimate the time based on message timestamps if I later asked it to stop. Instead, it suggested I use my phone's built-in Clock app.

Result: fail

2. Alarm

Strangely, I don't use alarms as much as stopwatches. But if I only have 25 minutes to spare, whether that’s for cleaning or working on a personal writing project, I'll sometimes set one to keep myself focused.

Would ChatGPT do any better here? Well, at first it looked promising. It created a scheduled task to notify me after 10 minutes. I checked that notifications were enabled, put my phone down and carried on working.

When I realized at least 15 minutes had passed, I checked the chat. Sure enough, ChatGPT had posted a message saying the time was up, but it hadn't actually alerted me. Later, I discovered it had also sent an email but it had landed in my spam folder. This one was a fail too in my book.

Result: fail

3. Word games

I love the word games in the New York Times app, home to addictive puzzles like Wordle and Connections. One of my current favorites is Spelling Bee. You're given a handful of letters and then have to make as many words as possible. It's one of my favorite ways to warm up my brain before I start writing.

Could ChatGPT recreate it? Surprisingly, yes. It generated a set of letters, understood the rules and kept track of the words I found. In terms of pure functionality, it worked.

But what it couldn't recreate was the experience. The New York Times app is beautifully simple, with an interface designed around the game. Playing through a chat window felt really clunky and annoying by comparison. The whole point of this game is I'm focusing on the letters and words, I don't want a constant back and forth with ChatGPT about the words.

So I'm calling this a partial success. Yes, ChatGPT replaced the mechanics of the game, but not the experience. And after a few rounds, I knew which version I'd rather use every day.

Result: partial pass

4. Star gazing

The Sky Guide app is one of my all-time favorites, especially its augmented reality mode. Turn on your phone's location and compass, point it at the night sky and it instantly tells you what you're looking at, whether that's constellations, planets, bits of debris, or the ISS. It's incredible.

Could ChatGPT replace it? Well, sort of. If you upload a photo of the night sky, ChatGPT can usually identify the constellations. But there are caveats. The image needs to be clear, the stars need to be visible and you're relying on a single snapshot. Whereas Sky Guide works continuously as you move your phone around the sky.

This was another reminder that knowledge doesn't necessarily bring you a good experience. Because yes, ChatGPT knows about constellations. But Sky Guide lets you explore them. You can point your phone in any direction, tap on a star or planet and instantly get more information about it without having to keep asking questions. It's a much more intuitive way to learn.

Result: partial pass

5. Weather

Telling me what to expect from the weather forecast for the day turned out to be one of ChatGPT's strongest categories.

The forecast was accurate and pulled from a reliable source, so I trusted the information it gave me. I did find myself asking follow-up questions for things like the hourly forecast and the chance of rain, which would have taken a single tap in a dedicated weather app.

It knew the answers and I trusted them, but getting to them was much slower. That's why I'm generously calling this one a pass.

Result: pass

6. Guided meditation

I have a few favorite apps I use for guided meditations and have some saved in Spotify too. So I wondered whether ChatGPT could take over that role.

For this test, I switched on voice mode and asked it to guide me through a short meditation. Now, technically it did that. But in practice it wasn't even remotely relaxing.

Thanks to a recent update, the voice had odd intonation, frequent vocal fry and distracting little "ums", "ahs" and "let me sees" throughout that constantly pulled me out of the experience. At one point it even told me to breathe in, then never got around to telling me to breathe out.

By the logic of how I graded the other tests, this one should have been a partial pass. It did what I asked, right? But because I had to stop using it out of irritation and came away from the mediation feeling actively more stressed, it's going down as a fail for me.

Result: fail

7. Calculator

ChatGPT doesn't have a great track record of counting things, so I was wary about using it as a calculator. I asked it to do some massive sums for me and it got all of them right.

It did pause a few times with a "let me think" message, so I wasn't getting the instant response I'd expect from a calculator. But the delay was only a few seconds, and the answers were correct.

Once again, I found myself missing the simplicity of an app. Typing numbers into a calculator is faster than turning them into a conversation. But ChatGPT did work as a capable stand-in.

Result: pass

8. Movie recommendations

I love Letterboxd. I log every film I watch, browse other people's lists and regularly discover new films through recommendations.

Now, there was never a chance ChatGPT could replace the logging side of the app. It can't update my Letterboxd diary or plug me into that community. But recommendations are one of the main reasons I use it, so I wondered how well ChatGPT would do.

I asked it to recommend films similar to some of my favorites, then spent the next few evenings watching its suggestions to really test them. And, to my surprise, it did an excellent job.

Then again, that perhaps isn't all that surprising. We know LLMs are trained on huge amounts of publicly available text, especially discussions reviews and recommendations from where film fans gather online, like Reddit. But whatever the reason, the recommendations felt well matched to my taste.

What I missed wasn't the recommendations themselves, but the social side of Letterboxd. I do enjoy seeing what friends had watched, reading reviews and stumbling across unexpected lists. So, for me, ChatGPT can't replace Letterboxd, but for simply finding something to watch, it did well.

Result: pass

9. Maps

I rely on my Maps app both for planning journeys in advance and for live navigation. So I asked ChatGPT the best way to get from my home to the airport the following day.

At first, it handled the request well. It laid out the different travel options clearly under headings and the advice looked really sensible. It even cited sources from places like Rome2Rio and The Trainline.

Then things got unnecessarily complicated. At the end of those suggestions it asked what time my flight was so it could tailor the recommendations. But when I told it, it started creating a scheduled task instead. I didn't want a reminder, so I had to cancel that, explain what I actually meant and steer the conversation back to route planning.

Eventually, it gave me the information I wanted. But the Maps app would have got me there in a fraction of the time, without all the back and forth.

It also can't replace what I actually use Maps for the most, which is live, turn-by-turn navigation.

Result: partial pass

10. Food delivery

ChatGPT obviously can't deliver food, but I wondered whether it could replace the part of the app I probably spend the longest on, which is deciding what to eat.

It got off to a surprisingly good start. It asked about my preferences, budget and location, then narrowed down the options and even presented them neatly on a map.

The recommendations themselves looked really good. They're all local places I already really liked to eat at. But there was just one problem. Every restaurant it suggested was closed. Even the map it generated had "closed" written beneath each one.

After a bit of back and forth, it said they weren't shut, eventually acknowledged that they were and suggested a different set of places instead.

Unfortunately, those weren't much use either. They were small independent cafés and restaurants that don't appear on food delivery apps. I wouldn't expect ChatGPT to know exactly which businesses partner with which delivery services, but it did highlight the gap between recommending somewhere to eat and actually helping me make a decision about where I could order from.

Result: fail

11. Language learning

I still very reluctantly use Duolingo and have recently started trialling a few other language learning apps to polish my Spanish.

I asked ChatGPT to help me improve my Spanish for an upcoming trip and it suggested role-play ordering food in a café so I could practise.

We switched to voice mode and at first it felt genuinely fun. It held a natural back-and-forth conversation and felt much closer to speaking to a real person than working through a series of multiple-choice questions like in Duolingo.

But it was also noticeably glitchier than a dedicated language app thanks to that recent voice update. There were odd pauses in the conversation, and at one point it repeatedly kept marking one of my answers as incorrect when it wasn't. Shortly afterwards, the exercise just stopped working altogether after a bizarre "ummmmm" from ChatGPT.

When it was working, I actually enjoyed the experience more than using an app like Duolingo. But if I'm trying to learn a language properly, I also want something that's reliable.

Result: partial pass

12. Plant identification

I love identifying things I see in nature, like bird song with the Merlin app. But I most often rely on plant identifying apps when I'm walking to take a quick snap of a leaf or flower then find out more about it.

ChatGPT was really effective at doing this. I took pictures of leaves, trees, flowers and bushes. I was a little wary about the results at first because I know that ChatGPT tends to make guesses about things rather than admitting it doesn't know. But I did fact check all of the results and everything seemed accurate.

Again, I missed some of the simple, additional features in dedicated apps. But it was surprisingly effective.

Result: pass

Can AI really replace your apps?

Before drawing too many conclusions, it's worth pointing out that a true AI-native phone wouldn't just be ChatGPT running as another app like it was in this experiment. It would probably be integrated into the operating system. Which would mean it could access things like your calendars, timers, navigation and settings. So many of the tasks ChatGPT failed at here might become a whole lot easier with an AI-first phone.

This experiment was based on whether AI could replace the apps on my phone. What I found was that it replaces a specific kind of app. Well, sort of.

If an app's main job is providing information, explaining something or answering questions, AI is already a fairly capable alternative. Plant identification, travel advice, calculations and general knowledge all felt natural.

But if an app exists to perform an action quickly, like starting a timer, setting an alarm, finding restaurants for getting food delivered, opening a map, AI still has a long way to go. Those tasks depend on deeper integration with the device and a different way of working, not just how smart it is.

There are some big trade-offs, too. Dedicated apps often rely on specialist databases and expertise, while AI can still present incorrect answers confidently or fail to make its uncertainty clear. For example, when I was trying to identify a plant I felt wary because I'd generally trust an app built with the input of botanists over a chatbot.

And, as you could probably tell from my mounting frustration, a huge sticking point for me was also realizing how much I missed the interface of many apps.

For me, a well-designed app is always a better way to explore information than a conversation. I don't think everything should, or even can, be done through chat, despite that being the direction many AI companies seem to be heading. In fact, it showed me that a conversational interface can be more work rather than less.

It's impossible to know exactly what Apple and OpenAI's long-term plans are. But I can imagine a future where knowledge apps increasingly merge into AI, while utility apps remain part of the operating system itself.

If that happens, we may stop thinking about which app to open and simply ask AI instead. But for that future to actually catch one, I'd want stronger guarantees around accuracy, better integration with trusted sources and the option to step outside the chat interface more often.

She’s been writing about consumer tech and popular science for more than ten years, covering all kinds of topics, including why robots have eyes and whether we’ll experience the overview effect one day. She’s particularly interested in VR/AR, wearables, digital health, space tech and chatting to experts and academics about the future. She’s contributed to TechRadar, T3, Wired, New Scientist, The Guardian, Inverse and many more. Her first book, Screen Time, came out in January 2021 with Bonnier Books. She loves science-fiction, brutalist architecture, and spending too much time floating through space in virtual reality.

blocks.html_en: 1. Stopwatch

sentences.en: Stopwatch

sentences.zh: （图片来源：Shutterstock / Lee Bryant Photography）

blocks.html_en: I use the stopwatch in my iPhone's Clock app constantly throughout the day. When you can set your own schedule, it's way too easy to disappear down a research rabbit hole and lose an hour.

sentences.en: I use the stopwatch in my iPhone's Clock app constantly throughout the day.

sentences.zh: 它说它无法测量经过的时间，尽管如果我后来要求它停止，它可以根据消息时间戳估计时间。

sentences.zh: （图片来源：Shutterstock / Terang Bulan Gallery）

blocks.html_en: Strangely, I don't use alarms as much as stopwatches. But if I only have 25 minutes to spare, whether that’s for cleaning or working on a personal writing project, I'll sometimes set one to keep myself focused.

sentences.en: Strangely, I don't use alarms as much as stopwatches.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，我使用闹钟的次数不如秒表。

blocks.html_en: Would ChatGPT do any better here? Well, at first it looked promising. It created a scheduled task to notify me after 10 minutes. I checked that notifications were enabled, put my phone down and carried on working.

sentences.en: Would ChatGPT do any better here?
sentences.zh: ChatGPT 在这里会做得更好吗？

sentences.en: When I realized at least 15 minutes had passed, I checked the chat.
sentences.zh: 当我意识到至少已经过去了 15 分钟时，我查看了聊天记录。

sentences.en: Sure enough, ChatGPT had posted a message saying the time was up, but it hadn't actually alerted me.
sentences.zh: 果然，ChatGPT 发了一条消息说时间到了，但实际上并没有提醒我。

sentences.en: This one was a fail too in my book.

blocks.html_en: 3. Word games

sentences.en: Word games
sentences.zh: 文字游戏

sentences.en: (Image credit: Shutterstock / Iuliana Ionescu)
sentences.zh: （图片来源：Shutterstock / Iuliana Ionescu）

blocks.html_en: I love the word games in the New York Times app, home to addictive puzzles like Wordle and Connections. One of my current favorites is Spelling Bee. You're given a handful of letters and then have to make as many words as possible. It's one of my favorite ways to warm up my brain before I start writing.

sentences.en: I love the word games in the New York Times app, home to addictive puzzles like Wordle and Connections.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢《纽约时报》应用程序中的文字游戏，其中有 Wordle 和 Connections 等令人上瘾的谜题。

sentences.en: One of my current favorites is Spelling Bee.
sentences.zh: 我目前最喜欢的活动之一是拼字比赛。

sentences.en: You're given a handful of letters and then have to make as many words as possible.
sentences.zh: 你会得到一些字母，然后必须拼出尽可能多的单词。

sentences.en: It's one of my favorite ways to warm up my brain before I start writing.
sentences.zh: 这是我开始写作之前最喜欢的预热大脑的方法之一。

blocks.html_en: Could ChatGPT recreate it? Surprisingly, yes. It generated a set of letters, understood the rules and kept track of the words I found. In terms of pure functionality, it worked.

sentences.en: Could ChatGPT recreate it?
sentences.zh: ChatGPT 可以重新创建它吗？

sentences.en: Surprisingly, yes.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，是的。

sentences.en: It generated a set of letters, understood the rules and kept track of the words I found.
sentences.zh: 它生成了一组字母，理解规则并记录我找到的单词。

sentences.en: In terms of pure functionality, it worked.
sentences.zh: 就纯粹的功能而言，它是有效的。

blocks.html_en: But what it couldn't recreate was the experience. The New York Times app is beautifully simple, with an interface designed around the game. Playing through a chat window felt really clunky and annoying by comparison. The whole point of this game is I'm focusing on the letters and words, I don't want a constant back and forth with ChatGPT about the words.

sentences.en: But what it couldn't recreate was the experience.
sentences.zh: 但它无法重现的是体验。

sentences.en: The New York Times app is beautifully simple, with an interface designed around the game.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序非常简单，界面围绕游戏设计。

sentences.en: Playing through a chat window felt really clunky and annoying by comparison.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，通过聊天窗口玩游戏感觉真的很笨重而且烦人。

sentences.en: The whole point of this game is I'm focusing on the letters and words, I don't want a constant back and forth with ChatGPT about the words.
sentences.zh: 这个游戏的重点是我专注于字母和单词，我不想与 ChatGPT 不断地来回讨论单词。

blocks.html_en: So I'm calling this a partial success. Yes, ChatGPT replaced the mechanics of the game, but not the experience. And after a few rounds, I knew which version I'd rather use every day.

sentences.en: So I'm calling this a partial success.
sentences.zh: 所以我称这是部分成功。

sentences.en: Yes, ChatGPT replaced the mechanics of the game, but not the experience.
sentences.zh: 是的，ChatGPT 取代了游戏的机制，但没有取代体验。

sentences.en: And after a few rounds, I knew which version I'd rather use every day.
sentences.zh: 经过几轮之后，我知道我每天更愿意使用哪个版本。

blocks.html_en: 4. Star gazing

sentences.en: Star gazing
sentences.zh: 观星

sentences.en: (Image credit: Shutterstock / Milosz_G)
sentences.zh: （图片来源：Shutterstock / Milosz_G）

blocks.html_en: The Sky Guide app is one of my all-time favorites, especially its augmented reality mode. Turn on your phone's location and compass, point it at the night sky and it instantly tells you what you're looking at, whether that's constellations, planets, bits of debris, or the ISS. It's incredible.

sentences.en: The Sky Guide app is one of my all-time favorites, especially its augmented reality mode.
sentences.zh: Sky Guide 应用程序是我一直以来的最爱之一，尤其是它的增强现实模式。

sentences.en: Turn on your phone's location and compass, point it at the night sky and it instantly tells you what you're looking at, whether that's constellations, planets, bits of debris, or the ISS.
sentences.zh: 打开手机的位置和指南针，将其指向夜空，它会立即告诉您所看到的内容，无论是星座、行星、碎片还是国际空间站。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

blocks.html_en: Could ChatGPT replace it? Well, sort of. If you upload a photo of the night sky, ChatGPT can usually identify the constellations. But there are caveats. The image needs to be clear, the stars need to be visible and you're relying on a single snapshot. Whereas Sky Guide works continuously as you move your phone around the sky.

sentences.en: Could ChatGPT replace it?
sentences.zh: ChatGPT 可以取代它吗？

sentences.en: Well, sort of.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有点像。

sentences.en: If you upload a photo of the night sky, ChatGPT can usually identify the constellations.
sentences.zh: 如果您上传夜空照片，ChatGPT 通常可以识别星座。

sentences.en: But there are caveats.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些警告。

sentences.en: The image needs to be clear, the stars need to be visible and you're relying on a single snapshot.
sentences.zh: 图像需要清晰，星星需要可见，并且您依赖的是单个快照。

sentences.en: Whereas Sky Guide works continuously as you move your phone around the sky.
sentences.zh: 而当您在天空中移动手机时，Sky Guide 会持续工作。

blocks.html_en: This was another reminder that knowledge doesn't necessarily bring you a good experience. Because yes, ChatGPT knows about constellations. But Sky Guide lets you explore them. You can point your phone in any direction, tap on a star or planet and instantly get more information about it without having to keep asking questions. It's a much more intuitive way to learn.

sentences.en: This was another reminder that knowledge doesn't necessarily bring you a good experience.
sentences.zh: 这再次提醒我们，知识并不一定会给你带来良好的体验。

sentences.en: Because yes, ChatGPT knows about constellations.
sentences.zh: 因为是的，ChatGPT 了解星座。

sentences.en: But Sky Guide lets you explore them.
sentences.zh: 但 Sky Guide 可以让您探索它们。

sentences.en: You can point your phone in any direction, tap on a star or planet and instantly get more information about it without having to keep asking questions.
sentences.zh: 您可以将手机指向任何方向，点击一颗恒星或行星，即可立即获得有关它的更多信息，而无需继续提问。

sentences.en: It's a much more intuitive way to learn.
sentences.zh: 这是一种更直观的学习方式。

sentences.en: Weather

sentences.zh: （图片来源：Shutterstock / Kaspars Grinvalds）

blocks.html_en: Telling me what to expect from the weather forecast for the day turned out to be one of ChatGPT's strongest categories.

sentences.en: Telling me what to expect from the weather forecast for the day turned out to be one of ChatGPT's strongest categories.
sentences.zh: 告诉我当天的天气预报是 ChatGPT 最强的类别之一。

sentences.en: The forecast was accurate and pulled from a reliable source, so I trusted the information it gave me.

sentences.en: For this test, I switched on voice mode and asked it to guide me through a short meditation.

sentences.en: Thanks to a recent update, the voice had odd intonation, frequent vocal fry and distracting little "ums", "ahs" and "let me sees" throughout that constantly pulled me out of the experience.

blocks.html_en: I love Letterboxd. I log every film I watch, browse other people's lists and regularly discover new films through recommendations.

sentences.en: I love Letterboxd.

blocks.html_en: I asked it to recommend films similar to some of my favorites, then spent the next few evenings watching its suggestions to really test them. And, to my surprise, it did an excellent job.

sentences.en: I asked it to recommend films similar to some of my favorites, then spent the next few evenings watching its suggestions to really test them.
sentences.zh: 我要求它推荐与我最喜欢的一些电影类似的电影，然后在接下来的几个晚上观看它的建议以真正测试它们。

blocks.html_en: Then again, that perhaps isn't all that surprising. sentences.en: Then again, that perhaps isn't all that surprising.

sentences.en: We know LLMs are trained on huge amounts of publicly available text, especially discussions reviews and recommendations from where film fans gather online, like Reddit.
sentences.zh: 我们知道法学硕士接受过大量公开文本的培训，尤其是来自影迷在线聚集地（例如 Reddit）的评论和推荐的讨论。

content_html_zh:
苹果和 OpenAI 目前正在进行一场法律诉讼。 苹果指控 OpenAI 窃取商业机密并挖走员工。

但这两家公司的关系一直很复杂。 他们于 2024 年合作，将 ChatGPT 引入苹果设备，但苹果为 Siri 选择了谷歌的 Gemini，而不是 OpenAI。 随后 OpenAI 收购了苹果前设计总监 Jony Ive 创立的硬件初创公司 io，并承诺推出由 AI 驱动的未来硬件设备。

所有这些都引发了人们的猜测：如果 OpenAI 也生产硬件，苹果会担心什么。 我们无法了解该公司的动机，案件的具体情况仍在调查中。 但这让我开始思考，如果你的手机不再是应用程序的集合，而是围绕着人工智能，会怎样？

如果人工智能成为主要界面，哪些应用程序会消失，哪些应用程序会生存？ 通过 ChatGPT 控制的手机真的实用吗？

所以我决定根据我们现有的技术来找出答案。 有一天，每当我使用某个应用程序时，我都会先尝试 ChatGPT。 如果它能完成这项工作，那就太好了，它通过了测试。 如果做不到，那就失败了。

从一开始我就错过了一些明显的事情。 ChatGPT 未连接到我的电子邮件，它无法为我打开 WhatsApp，也无法访问我的钱包，因此这些不会成为测试的一部分。 但有很多日常任务感觉像是公平的游戏。

1. 跑表

我全天不断使用 iPhone 时钟应用程序中的秒表。 当我工作、做饭或锻炼时，这是我发现的让我作为自由职业者走上正轨的最简单的方法之一。 当你可以设定自己的时间表时，就很容易消失在研究兔子洞中并损失一个小时。

订阅突发新闻、评论、观点、顶级技术交易等。

我要求 ChatGPT 启动秒表。 它说它无法测量经过的时间，尽管如果我后来要求它停止，它可以根据消息时间戳估计时间。 相反，它建议我使用手机的内置时钟应用程序。

结果：失败

2. Alarm

奇怪的是，我使用闹钟的次数不如秒表。 但如果我只有 25 分钟的空闲时间，无论是打扫卫生还是从事个人写作项目，我有时会安排一个时间来让自己集中注意力。

ChatGPT 在这里会做得更好吗？ 嗯，一开始看起来很有希望。 它创建了一个计划任务，在 10 分钟后通知我。 我检查通知是否已启用，然后放下手机继续工作。

当我意识到至少已经过去了 15 分钟时，我查看了聊天记录。 果然，ChatGPT 发了一条消息说时间到了，但实际上并没有提醒我。 后来，我发现它也发送了一封电子邮件，但它已进入我的垃圾邮件文件夹。 这在我的书中也是失败的。

结果：失败

3. 文字游戏

我喜欢《纽约时报》应用程序中的文字游戏，其中有 Wordle 和 Connections 等令人上瘾的谜题。 我目前最喜欢的活动之一是拼字比赛。 你会得到一些字母，然后必须拼出尽可能多的单词。 这是我开始写作之前最喜欢的预热大脑的方法之一。

ChatGPT 可以重新创建它吗？ 令人惊讶的是，是的。 它生成了一组字母，理解规则并记录我找到的单词。 就纯粹的功能而言，它是有效的。

但它无法重现的是体验。 《纽约时报》应用程序非常简单，界面围绕游戏设计。 相比之下，通过聊天窗口玩游戏感觉真的很笨重而且烦人。 这个游戏的重点是我专注于字母和单词，我不想与 ChatGPT 不断地来回讨论单词。

所以我称这是部分成功。 是的，ChatGPT 取代了游戏的机制，但没有取代体验。 经过几轮之后，我知道我每天更愿意使用哪个版本。

结果：部分通过

4. 观星

Sky Guide 应用程序是我一直以来的最爱之一，尤其是它的增强现实模式。 打开手机的位置和指南针，将其指向夜空，它会立即告诉您所看到的内容，无论是星座、行星、碎片还是国际空间站。 太不可思议了。

ChatGPT 可以取代它吗？ 嗯，有点像。 如果您上传夜空照片，ChatGPT 通常可以识别星座。 但也有一些警告。 图像需要清晰，星星需要可见，并且您依赖的是单个快照。 而当您在天空中移动手机时，Sky Guide 会持续工作。

这再次提醒我们，知识并不一定会给你带来良好的体验。 因为是的，ChatGPT 了解星座。 但 Sky Guide 可以让您探索它们。 您可以将手机指向任何方向，点击一颗恒星或行星，即可立即获得有关它的更多信息，而无需继续提问。 这是一种更直观的学习方式。

结果：部分通过

5. 天气

告诉我当天的天气预报是 ChatGPT 最强的类别之一。

预测是准确的并且来自可靠的来源，所以我相信它给我的信息。 我确实发现自己在询问诸如每小时天气预报和下雨的可能性之类的后续问题，这些问题只需在专门的天气应用程序中点击一下即可。

它知道答案，我也相信它们，但找到答案要慢得多。 这就是为什么我慷慨地将其称为“通行证”。

结果：通过

6. 引导冥想

我有一些最喜欢的用于引导冥想的应用程序，也有一些保存在 Spotify 中。 所以我想知道 ChatGPT 是否可以接替这个角色。

在这次测试中，我打开了语音模式并要求它引导我进行短暂的冥想。 现在，从技术上讲，它做到了。 但实际上，这根本就没有放松。

由于最近的更新，声音有奇怪的语调，频繁的声音干扰和分散注意力的小“嗯”，“啊”和“让我看看”，这不断地将我从体验中拉出来。 有一次它甚至告诉我吸气，然后却再也没有时间告诉我呼气。

按照我对其他测试评分的逻辑，这一次应该是部分通过。 它按照我的要求做了，对吗？ 但因为我不得不因为恼怒而停止使用它，并且在结束调解后感觉压力更大，所以这对我来说是一个失败。

结果：失败

7. 计算器

ChatGPT 在计数方面没有很好的记录，因此我对将其用作计算器持谨慎态度。 我要求它为我做一些大笔的事情，它都做对了。

它确实暂停了几次，并显示“让我想想”消息，所以我没有得到计算器所期望的即时响应。 但仅仅延迟了几秒钟，答案就正确了。

我再一次发现自己怀念应用程序的简单性。 在计算器中输入数字比将其转化为对话要快。 但 ChatGPT 确实可以作为一个有能力的替代品。

结果：通过

8. 电影推荐

我喜欢 Letterboxd。 我记录我观看的每一部电影，浏览其他人的列表，并定期通过推荐发现新电影。

现在，ChatGPT 永远不可能取代应用程序的日志记录部分。 它无法更新我的 Letterboxd 日记或让我加入该社区。 但推荐是我使用它的主要原因之一，所以我想知道 ChatGPT 的表现如何。

我要求它推荐与我最喜欢的一些电影类似的电影，然后在接下来的几个晚上观看它的建议以真正测试它们。 而且，令我惊讶的是，它做得非常出色。

话又说回来，这也许并不令人惊讶。 我们知道法学硕士接受过大量公开文本的培训，尤其是来自影迷在线聚集地（例如 Reddit）的评论和推荐的讨论。 但无论出于什么原因，这些推荐感觉很符合我的口味。

我错过的不是推荐本身，而是 Letterboxd 的社交方面。 我确实喜欢看朋友们看过的内容、阅读评论以及偶然发现意想不到的列表。 所以，对我来说，ChatGPT 无法取代 Letterboxd，但对于简单地寻找可看的内容来说，它表现得很好。

结果：通过

9. Maps

我依靠地图应用程序提前规划行程和实时导航。 所以我询问 ChatGPT 第二天从我家到机场的最佳方式。

起初，它很好地处理了请求。 它在标题下清楚地列出了不同的旅行选择，并且建议看起来非常明智。 它甚至引用了来自 Rome2Rio 和 The Trainline 等地方的消息来源。

然后事情变得不必要的复杂。 在这些建议结束时，它询问我的航班时间，以便它可以定制建议。 但当我告诉它时，它开始创建一个计划任务。 我不想收到提醒，所以我不得不取消提醒，解释一下我的实际意思，并将谈话引回到路线规划上。

最终，它给了我我想要的信息。 但地图应用程序可以让我在很短的时间内到达那里，而不需要所有的来回。

它也无法取代我实际最常用的地图功能，即实时路线导航。

结果：部分通过

10. 送餐

ChatGPT 显然无法提供食物，但我想知道它是否可以取代应用程序中我可能花费最长时间的部分，即决定吃什么。

它有一个令人惊讶的良好开端。 它询问了我的偏好、预算和位置，然后缩小了选择范围，甚至将它们整齐地呈现在地图上。

这些建议本身看起来非常好。 它们都是我非常喜欢吃的当地地方。 但只有一个问题。 它建议的每家餐馆都关门了。 甚至它生成的地图在每张地图下面都写着“关闭”。

经过一番来回，它说他们没有关门，最终承认他们已经关门了，并建议换一个不同的地方。

不幸的是，这些也没有多大用处。 它们是小型独立咖啡馆和餐馆，不会出现在食品配送应用程序上。 我不希望 ChatGPT 确切地知道哪些企业与哪些送货服务合作，但它确实凸显了推荐吃饭的地方和实际帮助我决定可以从哪里订购之间的差距。

结果：失败

11. 语言学习

我仍然非常不情愿地使用 Duolingo，并且最近开始尝试其他一些语言学习应用程序来提高我的西班牙语水平。

我请求 ChatGPT 帮助我为即将到来的旅行提高西班牙语水平，它建议我进行角色扮演，在咖啡馆点餐，这样我就可以练习。

我们切换到语音模式，一开始感觉真的很有趣。 它进行了自然的来回对话，感觉更接近于与真人交谈，而不是像在 Duolingo 中那样解决一系列多项选择题。

但由于最近的语音更新，它也明显比专用语言应用程序更容易出现故障。 谈话中出现了奇怪的停顿，有一次它不断地将我的一个答案标记为不正确，而实际上它并不正确。 不久之后，在 ChatGPT 发出奇怪的“ummmmm”之后，该练习就完全停止了。

当它运行时，我实际上比使用 Duolingo 这样的应用程序更享受这种体验。 但如果我想正确地学习一门语言，我也想要一些可靠的东西。

结果：部分通过

12. 植物鉴定

我喜欢识别我在大自然中看到的事物，例如使用 Merlin 应用程序识别鸟鸣声。 但当我走路时，我最常依赖植物识别应用程序快速拍摄叶子或花朵，然后了解更多信息。

ChatGPT 在这方面确实非常有效。 我拍了树叶、树木、花朵和灌木丛的照片。 起初我对结果有点警惕，因为我知道 ChatGPT 倾向于对事情进行猜测，而不是承认它不知道。 但我确实检查了所有结果，一切似乎都是准确的。

我再次错过了专用应用程序中的一些简单的附加功能。 但它的效果出奇的好。

结果：通过

人工智能真的能取代你的应用程序吗？

在得出太多结论之前，值得指出的是，真正的 AI 原生手机不会像本次实验那样只是将 ChatGPT 作为另一个应用程序运行。 它可能会集成到操作系统中。 这意味着它可以访问您的日历、计时器、导航和设置等内容。 ChatGPT 在这里失败的许多任务可能会因为人工智能优先的手机而变得容易得多。

这个实验是基于AI是否可以取代我手机上的应用程序。 我发现它取代了特定类型的应用程序。 嗯，有点像。

如果应用程序的主要工作是提供信息、解释某些内容或回答问题，那么人工智能已经是一个相当有能力的替代方案。 植物识别、旅行建议、计算和常识都感觉很自然。

但如果有一个应用程序能够快速执行某项操作，比如启动计时器、设置闹钟、寻找送餐餐厅、打开地图，那么人工智能还有很长的路要走。 这些任务取决于与设备的更深入集成以及不同的工作方式，而不仅仅是它的智能程度。

也有一些重大的权衡。 专用应用程序通常依赖于专业数据库和专业知识，而人工智能仍然可以自信地给出错误答案或无法明确其不确定性。 例如，当我试图识别一种植物时，我感到很谨慎，因为我通常会信任由植物学家的输入构建的应用程序，而不是聊天机器人。

而且，正如你可能从我不断增加的挫败感中看出的那样，对我来说一个巨大的症结还在于意识到我是多么怀念许多应用程序的界面。

对我来说，设计精良的应用程序始终是比对话更好的探索信息的方式。 我认为并不是所有事情都应该、甚至可以通过聊天来完成，尽管这似乎是许多人工智能公司的发展方向。 事实上，它向我展示了对话界面可以增加工作量，而不是减少工作量。

我们不可能确切知道苹果和 OpenAI 的长期计划是什么。 但我可以想象未来知识应用程序将越来越多地融入人工智能，而实用程序应用程序仍然是操作系统本身的一部分。

如果发生这种情况，我们可能会不再考虑打开哪个应用程序，而是直接询问人工智能。 但为了让未来真正抓住这一机会，我希望在准确性方面有更强有力的保证，与可信来源更好地集成，以及更频繁地走出聊天界面的选项。
